origin: Independent third-party historical UART; not an injected defect
behavior: Synchronous positive reset holds busy and returns serial output high. BREAK forces serial low and busy high; after release allow at least 16 baud intervals of recovery.

CTS is active low. When setup[30] is zero, a receiver that has blocked continuously for at least eight clocks must not see busy go low or a new byte accepted. CTS changes have synchronizer latency. An in-flight byte may finish.

With CTS permissive (or setup[30]=1), pending bytes must eventually be accepted after reset/BREAK recovery and emitted as start=0, least-significant data bit first, configured parity, then one or two high stop bits.
A byte is accepted on a clock edge with i_wr && !o_busy, outside reset and BREAK. A source sends only one-clock write strobes when not busy.
Configuration is constant for an entire run. Tested divisors are at least four, data widths five through eight, parity disabled or fixed mark/space, one or two stop bits.

setup_fields.24: With fixed parity: 1=mark, 0=space. Computed parity mode excluded.

scope: Black-box external port checks at explicit configurations. Initial qualification found divisor-two forward-progress failure and computed-parity disagreement even in maintainer-fixed RTL; both remain recorded and are excluded from this CTS-specific contract. No fixed-RTL equivalence, CDC/metastability, physical board, all-configuration or unbounded claim.
